name: Control — random side, every game
role: CONTROL. Never eligible for a reward; its only job is to be the floor.
rule: For every game on the slate, take a side by a coin flip fixed in advance by the game_id hash. Stake 1 unit at -110.

registration.note: control, not a hypothesis; no result may be used to tune it

expected_from_control: break-even hit rate 52.38%; any edge over this must survive G4 and G5 before it is called skill
what_would_change_our_mind: Nothing. A control that starts beating the field means the scoring, not the control, is broken.

name: Control — favourites only
role: CONTROL. The most common 'system' in sports betting; included so it is measured, not assumed.
rule: Bet the side with the higher published win-differential, at -110, in every game where a market price exists.
inputs: official standings W-L (S03) at the time of the bet
expected_from_control: a record-based rule is public information; if it beat the market consistently, the market would already move
what_would_change_our_mind: Sustained positive CLV on a pre-registered, frozen version. A season of profit alone would not.

name: Scoring-margin baseline (PF-PA per game)
role: CANDIDATE. Deliberately the simplest strength model: if a complex model cannot beat this, it is not earning its complexity.
rule: Rating = (PF - PA) / games played, from the official league table, computed only from games completed before the kickoff being forecast. Home-side rating difference plus a fixed home-field constant of 3.0 points is the fair spread.
inputs: official PF, PA, W, L, T per club (S03 at the time of the bet)

registration.note: rule text above is the freeze candidate; it is not yet committed as a hash-pinned registration

power_note: needs 1,540 scored forecasts to detect a 55% vs 52.4% edge at 80% power
what_would_change_our_mind: BSS lower bound below zero for two consecutive registered windows; or the Elo model beating it on the same window by more than the interval width.

name: Causal Elo (fl1-elo-v1), frozen
role: CANDIDATE. Exists in this repository as a model version string; it has never been scored against a benchmark.
rule: Elo with K=20, home-field 48 rating points, inter-season regression x0.75 toward 1505, margin-of-victory multiplier. Spread = 10.8*log10(p/(1-p)). Version string recorded per row in data/fair_lines.csv.
inputs: game results before kickoff only (causal), from the official results feed

registration.note: the version string is recorded per row, but no commit hash freezes the code that produced it

what_would_change_our_mind: It is beaten on the same window by the PF-PA baseline; the spread constant (10.8) is not validated against a price, only against itself.

name: Availability-surprise overlay
role: CANDIDATE. The brief's central modelling idea: an injury signal must be a surprise, never a level.
rule: For each club, compute an availability index as the sum over unavailable starters of a *string gap*, and forecast the change in the index between the last pre-kickoff snapshot and the season average. A club whose index is worse than its own trailing distribution is a candidate; the size of the deviation, not the count of injured players, is the input.
inputs: official injury report snapshots (S89 for the Week 10 capture), club depth charts with their source ids, and the published designation

registration.note: blocked: needs at least two dated pre-kickoff snapshots per game, which the repository does not yet hold

blocking_gate: D5-G2 and D5-G3: no snapshot pair exists for any game, so no forecast can be scored
what_would_change_our_mind: An ablation that shows the personnel features add nothing to BSS on chronological holdouts (that ablation is registered as D5S11).

name: Two-leg game parlay (side + total, different games)
role: CANDIDATE. Cross-game, so independence is *approximately* defensible — but it is an assumption, not a validated fact.
rule: Combine the best-ranked side from one game with the best-ranked total from another, when both legs independently clear G4.

registration.note: not registered: no leg has cleared G4 yet

joint_validation.detail: the product of two marginals is used as the joint; no realised joint outcome has been checked against it

what_would_change_our_mind: A measured cross-game correlation whose upper bound is below the level at which multiplying marginals is unbiased.

name: Same-game parlay (side + total, one game)
role: CANDIDATE, gated. Multiplication of marginals is invalid here, and the repository says so everywhere.
rule: Combine a side and a total in the same game. Only rankable when a directly validated joint probability exists.

registration.note: not registered: blocked by its own gate

joint_validation.detail: side and total in the same game share pace and script; the product of their marginals is not the joint

what_would_change_our_mind: A directly estimated joint probability from realised same-game outcomes that beats the product of the marginals by more than its interval.

name: Player-prop combo (QB passing + WR receiving)
role: CANDIDATE, gated. The repository already publishes an empirical QB-WR correlation from an in-repo dataset (flagged third-party).
rule: Combine a QB passing-yards over with the same team's WR1 receiving-yards over. Use the measured correlation, not independence.
inputs: third-party player-week stats (flagged; not an official NFL feed) and the operator's prop rules

registration.note: not registered: the input feed is third-party and flagged

joint_validation.detail: the correlation is measured, but a measured marginal correlation is not a validated joint probability for the pair of lines actually being priced

what_would_change_our_mind: A joint model calibrated on realised joint outcomes, with the operator's void rules applied, clearing its own Brier test.

name: REJECTED — rank by season-long ROI
role: REJECTED by the brief itself. Kept in the register so the rejection is visible, not silent.
rule: Rank strategies by realised return over the season.

registration.note: rejected before evaluation, which is the correct time to reject a rule

rejection_reason: Season-long ROI is dominated by variance at this sample size: one 5-unit dog at +400 moves a whole-season number more than a real 2% edge over 100 bets. It is a staking statistic masquerading as a skill statistic.
what_would_change_our_mind: Nothing on this timeline. It could be revisited only as a secondary display once G4 is passed by a pre-registered rule.

name: REJECTED — derive depth order from jersey number, experience or salary
role: REJECTED. It is the tempting shortcut that would fabricate a starter the club never named.
rule: Infer the starter at each slot from roster attributes on the official roster page.
rejection_reason: Jersey order is not depth order. The repository already carried the counter-example: a rank-1 player who is a veteran backup, and clubs that list three rank-1 receivers.
what_would_change_our_mind: An official league-wide depth publication with dated slots. None exists at nfl.com/depth-charts/ (F02).

name: Ablation — personnel features on vs off
role: CANDIDATE (method). The brief asks for ablations instead of fixed point penalties; this is that ablation, registered as its own entry.
rule: Run the identical singles model twice, once with verified availability features and once without, on the same chronological holdouts. Report the BSS difference with its game-cluster interval. A fixed 'starter out = -2 points' penalty is forbidden.
what_would_change_our_mind: A difference interval that spans zero: then the personnel features are not earning their data cost, and should be dropped rather than tuned.
